capability.name: What a site's robots.txt lets each AI agent do, and what it signals
capability.description: Reads https://<host>/robots.txt and applies RFC 9309 as HISTOR's crawler does: the group naming each product token (else *), the longest matching rule with Allow winning a tie, percent-encoding normalised, * and $; 4xx means everything allowed, 5xx or no answer everything disallowed, same-host redirects followed. Answers, for a path and a list of agents (default: GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot, CCBot, Bytespider, Applebot-Extended, meta-externalagent, Amazonbot, histor and *), allowed or not, the deciding rule and group, and the group's Content-Signal (search, ai-input, ai-train). Also the groups, sitemaps and whether /llms.txt exists. A robots.txt is the site's request, not access control.

url.description: a domain or an https URL

path.description: the path to judge (default: the URL's)

note: before an agent fetches a page: what did the site ask agents to do
